column1: # BORU Language Specification: scalar edge cases 1 — the numeric tower
# Edge coverage for the four numeric leaves (Integer, Float, BigInteger,
# BigDecimal): cross-leaf equality vs ordering vs deep-equality, leaf
# promotion in every arithmetic word, int64 overflow at the literal and
# runtime boundaries, div/mod semantics on negative operands and at the
# int64 poles, and the two rounding regimes (round = ties away from
# zero, round-even = IEEE ties-to-even). Complements arithmetic.tsv,
# here pin the gaps those files leave. See
# §1  cross-leaf equality: eq / deq / cmp all treat equal magnitude as
#     equal across Integer/Float — deq is NOT stricter for scalars.

column3: deq agrees with eq across the Integer/Float leaves (magnitude, not leaf identity)
negative cross-leaf deq
Integer zero equals Float negative zero
deq across BigInteger/Integer is magnitude too
deq across BigDecimal/Float (1.5 is binary-exact)
trailing BigDecimal scale does not affect equality
Float 0.1 is really 0.1000…055…, strictly ABOVE exact 0d0.1 (big.Rat compare)
mirror: the exact decimal sorts below the binary Float
deq never coerces across families

column1: # §2  the 2^53 boundary — Integer/Float comparison projects to float64,
#     Big comparison is exact (big.Rat). Same magnitude, two answers.

column3: 2^53+1 as an Integer literal is exact (Phase 0a lexer)
stays an Integer, not a Float fallback
Integer/Float eq projects to float64 — 2^53+1 collapses onto 2^53
BigInteger/Float eq is exact — the same pair is NOT equal via big.Rat
a FLOAT literal above 2^53 rounds to the nearest representable

column1: # §3  leaf promotion in every arithmetic word (widest exact leaf wins;
#     bignum.tsv pins the add/mul basics — these are the gaps).

column3: BigInteger sub Integer stays Big
Integer sub BigInteger promotes; canon renders the sign outside 0d
Integer mod BigInteger → BigInteger
BigInteger mod Integer → BigInteger
cross-leaf integer division still truncates
BigDecimal div Integer → context division (decimal128)
Integer base, BigInteger exponent → BigInteger
BigInteger base, Integer exponent → BigInteger
Integer sub BigDecimal → BigDecimal
Big ⊕ Float never degrades: sub raises type_error (add/mul pinned in bignum.tsv)
…and div raises the same type_error

column1: # §4  int64 overflow — the literal boundary (statically flagged) and the
#     values via do/error so the CODE is pinned, not just the raise).

column3: int64 max literal is exact
int64 min literal is exact
one above max: the literal itself is range-checked
one below min likewise
binary literals are range-checked too (this is 2^63; the hex twin is pinned in numeric-cross-product.tsv)
runtime overflow carries the integer_overflow code
pow overflow carries the same code (no silent wrap)
minint mul -1 has no int64 result — checked, not wrapped
minint div -1 likewise — the division twin of the mul row
the BigInteger leaf is the overflow escape hatch

column1: # §5  the int64 poles under div/mod — minint div -1 is the ONE
#     division overflow (the true quotient 2^63 has no int64 home). It
#     now raises like the add/sub/mul/pow overflows (NUR006 fix — this
#     section previously pinned the Go-defined two's-complement wrap
#     as-is, the lone silent wrong answer left in integer arithmetic).
#     mod -1 stays 0: Go defines it, no overflow case exists for mod.

column3: minint div -1 raises — checked like every other integer overflow
minint mod -1 is 0 (no overflow)
reaching minint exactly is fine

column1: # §6  div/mod on double negatives (single-negative pairs are pinned in

column3: both operands negative: truncation toward zero gives +3
mod sign still follows the dividend
Float mod keeps the fraction and the dividend sign
a Float zero divisor routes the mixed pair to IEEE -inf
Integer 0 over Float 0.0 is IEEE nan, not an error

column1: # §7  pow edges not in the cross product

column3: 0^0 is 1 on the integer path
…and 1.0 on the Float path (IEEE pow(0,0)=1)
IEEE: pow(x, 0) is 1 even for x = inf
…and even for NaN
a Float base admits a negative Integer exponent (real reciprocal)
IEEE: pow(+0, negative) is +inf

column1: # §8  the two rounding regimes — round ties AWAY from zero, round-even
#     ties to even (IEEE roundTiesToEven); floor/ceil are directional.
#     All four are Float-typed: an Integer input is a dispatch error.

column3: round: 0.5 goes AWAY from zero
round: -0.5 goes away from zero too (not toward -inf)
round: -2.5 → -3 (away)
round-even: 0.5 ties to the even neighbour 0
round-even: -2.5 ties to even -2 (round gives -3)
round-even: 1.5 → 2 (2 is even)
round-even: 3.5 → 4 — adjacent halves land on DIFFERENT sides
floor is toward -inf
ceil is toward +inf
ceil of a small negative is zero
trunc is toward zero (compare floor: -3)
trunc positive
the rounding family returns an Integer, not a Float
the rounding family is total over Number — an Integer is already integral (identity; NUR008 fix — this row previously pinned the Float-only gap as an uncalled_function)
